event.cause: Indra’s attraction during the festival and encounter with Durvasas.
event.details: Dakṣa requests origins and battles of eight incarnations; Mudgala begins Vakratunda. Indra’s annual accession festival assembles the named gods, sages, attendants and musicians recorded in mud-e-festival-roster. Rambhā’s performance and ball play enthrall Indra, who closes it prematurely. After forest play with Rambhā, seeing Durvāsas makes him leave her and bow; his seed falls on earth. He returns home, repeatedly condemns his distraction and resumes his own dharma. Matsara arises from his seed; Earth nurtures, names and initiates him at five. He studies Vedas with an unnamed teacher, and marries Durbuddhi’s daughter Madakarā.
event.outcome: Matsara reaches adulthood and marriage.

event.cause: Matsara decides to conquer the cosmic egg by intense austerity.
event.details: Matsara obtains the five-syllable formula from Sukra and propitiates Sambhu. He stays in a secluded forest, observes Pasupata initiation, fasts for a thousand divine years, repeats the formula and meditates on Sadasiva. His austerity disturbs gods and beings. Gods and sages seek Sankara’s protection; Sankara comes with Parvati and his attendants. They see Matsara reduced to skin and bones, covered by an anthill.
event.outcome: Siva reaches the ascetic.

event.cause: Siva is pleased with Matsara’s austerity.
event.details: Siva awakens Matsara and invites his wishes. Matsara regains strength on seeing him, bows, worships and offers a hymn. After Siva renews the offer, Matsara asks for universal fearlessness, devotion, immunity from death caused by the five-element and three-guna domain, health with lasting lordship, and sovereignty over the cosmic egg. Although the request astonishes the assembly, Siva grants all of it because of the fierce austerity.
event.outcome: The requested compound boon is granted.

event.cause: Demons gathered at his father-in-law’s house seek conquest with his boon-supported strength.
event.details: The assembled demons urge Matsara to conquer the gods. He says that he wants this too, but Earth restrains him because Indra is his father and gods deserve honor. The demons counter with their own account of Jalandhara, argue that gods are enemies of demons, and tell Matsara to leave Earth. He accepts this advice, which the narrator calls harmful, abandons Earth and stays with them.
event.outcome: Matsara abandons Earth’s counsel and resides with the demons; the campaign follows in1.25.

event.details: Demons destroy Nāga gardens in Pātāla. Vāsuki, Takṣaka, Kambala and Aśvatara lead resistance: arms and missiles first repel demons; returning chiefs repel Nāgas. event.details: Demons proceed with captive Yama to Amarāvatī. Agni, Vāyu, Viśvedevas, Sādhyas, Rudras, Vasus, Gandharvas, Yakṣas, Vidyādharas, planets, moon, sun and Ādityas join Indra on Airāvata with vajra. event.details: Fleeing gods ask Kaśyapa to protect them and release Indra. With Vasiṣṭha, gods and sages, Kaśyapa petitions Brahmā to restore proper stations. Brahmā admits Matsara’s Śiva-boon makes him unconquerable and takes them to Viṣṇu, who also admits inability. They seek Śiva, who explains his own fierce-austerity grant and inability to destroy the demon. Viṣṇu chooses refuge at Kailāsa rather than submission, predicts Matsara will take Vaikuṇṭha and Satyaloka but spare Kailāsa out of devotion. Śiva remains anxious.
event.outcome: Gods cluster at Kailāsa; their expectation will be challenged.

event.details: Matsara occupies Indra’s throne, uses Airāvata, receives frightened celestial entertainers and redistributes divine offices to demon chiefs. He resents Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Rudra not paying homage. Andhaka is sent to summon them under threat, finds Satyaloka and Vaikuṇṭha empty, then enters Kailāsa and receives a seat.
